topics.title: United Kingdom Citizenship Requirements
topics.summary: The ordinary adult British naturalisation route: residence, settlement, absence limits, language evidence and the Life in the UK requirement.
topics.scope: Selected requirements for ordinary adult naturalisation under section 6(1), not the separate British-spouse route, registration, descent or Crown-service exceptions.

facts.label: Five-year residence route
facts.text: The ordinary route requires five years of UK residence and presence in the UK exactly five years before the application is received. Immigration-law compliance and the detailed rules for permitted absences still apply.
facts.locator: Eligibility; Residency requirements; When to apply

constraint.cohort: Ordinary adult section 6(1) applicants, subject to presence, absence and immigration conditions

facts.label: Settlement before applying
facts.text: The usual route requires indefinite leave or settled status held for 12 months. The British-spouse route has different timing; qualifying pre-settled-status cases also need a separate assessment.
facts.locator: Eligibility and fees; If you have pre-settled status

facts.label: Absence limits
facts.text: The usual limits are 450 days abroad in the five-year period and 90 days in its final 12 months. Home Office discretion is conditional, not an automatic waiver.
facts.locator: Time spent outside the UK; Form AN section 5

facts.label: Language evidence and exemptions
facts.text: An approved English speaking-and-listening qualification at CEFR B1 or higher is one accepted route. Qualifying degrees and listed nationalities offer alternatives. Age 65 or over gives an exemption; qualifying long-term medical conditions require supporting evidence. Welsh and Scottish Gaelic are also recognised.
facts.locator: Sections 9.2 and 9.3

facts.label: Life in the UK and other conditions
facts.text: Applicants normally pass the Life in the UK test, meet the good-character requirement and intend to keep their main home in the UK. The knowledge requirements have age and medical exemptions. Naturalisation is not an entitlement.
facts.locator: Eligibility; Form AN sections 1, 8, 9 and 10

facts.label: Check both nationalities
facts.text: The UK permits dual nationality, but becoming British may affect an existing nationality under the other country's law. Check that law before applying.
facts.locator: Section 14.2

limits: These are selected eligibility conditions, not an approval guarantee or processing-time estimate.
Minors, spouses, registration routes, exceptional residence discretion and the evidence checklist require their own official guidance.

topics.title: Ireland Tax Residence and Foreign Income
topics.summary: Irish tax residence, ordinary residence and domicile are separate tests. Together they affect the treatment of Irish and foreign income.
topics.scope: Baseline individual income-tax context, not an assessment of domicile, treaty entitlement, remittance-basis eligibility or a special relief.

facts.label: Annual and two-year day tests
facts.text: Tax residence normally follows 183 or more days in a calendar year, or 280 or more across that year and the preceding year. A year with 30 days or fewer does not make you resident under these tests.
facts.locator: How to know if you are resident for tax purposes

facts.label: How days are counted
facts.text: Any part of a day normally counts. Revenue describes exceptions for staying airside and certain unavoidable departure delays. An arrival-year residence election is a separate, conditional option.
facts.locator: A day; Can you choose to be tax resident?

facts.label: Residence and domicile together
facts.text: A person who is both resident and domiciled in Ireland is generally taxed on worldwide income, subject to applicable treaty relief. Residence alone is not a complete description of every person's foreign-income treatment.
facts.locator: Overview

facts.label: Obligations can continue after departure
facts.text: Three consecutive resident tax years establish ordinary residence from the fourth year. It continues for three tax years after leaving, potentially extending income-tax obligations; Revenue lists exceptions for particular foreign income.
facts.locator: How to know if you are ordinarily resident for tax purposes

facts.label: Irish income can remain taxable
facts.text: Someone neither resident nor domiciled can still owe tax on Irish-source income and foreign employment income for duties performed in Ireland. Ordinary residence and domicile must also be checked rather than treating departure as automatic exemption.
facts.locator: Non-residents

limits: Domicile is not established by the passport shown on this page. Non-domiciled treatment, treaties and split-year relief need individual review.
This summary does not calculate tax rates, social insurance, capital taxes or filing liabilities.

topics.title: Canada Tax Residence and Foreign Income
topics.summary: Canada distinguishes factual residence, deemed residence and treaty non-residence when determining individual income-tax obligations.
topics.scope: Selected CRA individual-residence principles; not a personal residence determination, provincial calculation or review of departure taxes.

facts.label: Residential ties matter
facts.text: CRA examines all relevant circumstances. A home, spouse or common-law partner, and dependants in Canada are significant ties; the passport alone does not settle residence.
facts.locator: Paragraphs 1.8 and 1.10–1.15

facts.label: The 183-day rule is not the only test
facts.text: Without factual residence, sojourning in Canada for at least 183 days in a calendar year can establish deemed residence for the whole year. Not every presence is sojourning; treaty rules can override this result.
facts.locator: Paragraphs 1.30–1.33 and 1.37

facts.label: Foreign-income scope
facts.text: Factual residents generally face worldwide-income taxation for their resident part of the year. Deemed residents normally face it for the whole year. Applicable treaty tie-breakers can instead establish deemed non-residence.
facts.locator: Summary; paragraphs 1.32 and 1.37–1.39

facts.label: Canadian-source income after leaving
facts.text: Non-residents can owe Canadian tax on Canadian-source income. Withholding and return requirements depend on the income type; employment, business, rent and pensions do not all follow the same procedure. Tell Canadian payers your residence status and country.
facts.locator: Your tax obligations; Part XIII tax; Part I tax

limits: A day count or passport is not a substitute for checking residence facts and the applicable treaty.
Rates, provincial rules, departure deemed-disposition rules and special cohorts are outside this baseline.

topics.title: Hong Kong Tax Scope and Foreign Income
topics.summary: Hong Kong applies distinct salaries, profits and property tax rules. Non-residence or receiving money overseas does not by itself settle liability.
topics.scope: Selected Hong Kong individual employment, business and rental-income rules; not mainland Chinese taxation or an analysis of a multinational corporate structure.
topics.jurisdiction: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region: individual tax context

facts.label: Non-residents can owe tax
facts.text: Services performed in Hong Kong under employment or a service contract can create liability whether or not the person is resident. IRD treats non-residence as a factual question, not a passport category.
facts.locator: Opening guidance on non-resident individuals

facts.label: Overseas payment is not enough
facts.text: IRD's employer guidance includes remuneration from a non-Hong Kong company among reportable employee income, whether paid locally or abroad. That payment location alone is not an exemption; the applicable employment and relief rules still need assessment.
facts.locator: Income chargeable to Salaries Tax; non-Hong Kong company payments, IR56B items 11 and 13

facts.label: Business profits depend on source
facts.text: For a Hong Kong trade, profession or business, the ordinary profits-tax charge concerns profits arising in or derived from Hong Kong, excluding capital-asset sale profits. Both residents and non-residents can be liable; identifying source is fact-sensitive.
facts.locator: The Scope of the Charge

facts.label: Hong Kong rental income
facts.text: Letting Hong Kong property creates reporting and tax obligations. Owners must keep rental records, report income and notify liability when required. A received return must be completed even if there was no rental income.
facts.locator: Tax Obligations as a Property Owner

limits: This is not a claim that foreign income is always exempt or that holding an HKSAR passport establishes tax residence.
Treaty certificates, employee exemptions, corporate foreign-sourced income rules, rates and special regimes are outside this selected individual baseline.

review.notes: Independently opened all 11 cited official sources and checked all 19 facts across GB citizenship and IE, CA and HK individual-tax topics against their stated locators. UK Form AN is the July 2026 edition; the ordinary section 6(1) route, conditional absence discretion, B1 as one accepted language-evidence route, alternative evidence, exemptions and other-nationality warning are preserved. Irish summaries correctly distinguish residence, ordinary residence and domicile and retain the 30-day condition, arrival-election qualification and continuing foreign-income exceptions. Canadian summaries preserve factual ties, sojourning rather than all presence, part-year versus deemed residence and treaty overrides; non-resident withholding and filing are not collapsed into one procedure. All four Hong Kong authorities returned current official HTML through independent direct HTTPS requests when the browser fetcher failed. Hong Kong employment, business and property claims are conditional and confined to the individual baseline; neither universal foreign-income exemption nor a corporate FSIE conclusion is asserted. Rechecked the requested HKSAR-passport terminology correction. Candidate schema passed. Approval covers these exact candidate bytes and selected factual scope only, not complete personal legal/tax advice, other research batches, rendering or deployment.

topics.title: Portugal Tax Residence and Foreign Income
topics.summary: Portugal's ordinary IRS rules distinguish residence, Portuguese-source income and foreign income, with important departure exceptions.
topics.scope: Selected individual IRS rules under Articles 15 and 16; not an eligibility assessment for NHR, IFICI, treaty relief or a personal tax calculation.

facts.label: Presence or a habitual home
facts.text: Residence can arise after more than 183 days in a relevant 12-month period beginning or ending in the income year. A shorter stay can qualify where an available dwelling indicates an intention to maintain and occupy it as a habitual home.
facts.locator: Article 16(1)(a)–(b)

facts.label: Overnight presence and part-year rules
facts.text: A counted day includes an overnight stay. Arrival and departure can create part-year residence, but statutory exceptions can extend it; residence is assessed separately for each household member.

facts.label: Resident income scope
facts.text: The ordinary rule taxes residents on income from Portugal and abroad. Article 15 applies the resident and non-resident scopes separately in qualifying part-year cases; special relief is not established by this baseline.
facts.locator: Article 15(1) and (3)

facts.label: Non-resident income scope
facts.text: For non-residents, IRS applies to Portuguese-source income. Leaving Portugal therefore does not automatically end every Portuguese income-tax obligation.
facts.locator: Article 15(2)–(3)

facts.label: A nationality-linked departure exception
facts.text: Portuguese nationals moving tax residence to a jurisdiction on the official favourable-tax list can remain resident for the departure year and four following years, unless an accepted justification is proved. The rule stops when residence moves outside that list.
facts.locator: Article 16(6)–(7)

limits: This page does not determine whether a destination is on the applicable official tax-jurisdiction list.
Treaties, special regimes, rates, social security and individual filing duties require separate review; a passport does not confer a preferential tax regime.

topics.title: France Tax Residence and Foreign Income
topics.summary: French tax residence depends on home, activity or economic interests, subject to treaties; it is not decided by a passport or a single day count.
topics.scope: Ordinary individual income-tax residence and income scope; excludes special public-service cases, impatriate relief and a personalised treaty assessment.

facts.label: Alternative residence tests
facts.text: Domestic residence can follow a French household home, or principal stay where there is no such home; a non-accessory professional activity in France; or the centre of economic interests there. These are alternatives, not cumulative requirements.
facts.locator: Article 4-B criteria in the main guidance

facts.label: Treaties can resolve dual residence
facts.text: Where two countries treat a person as resident, the applicable treaty can supply overriding residence criteria. The relevant treaty must be checked individually; without one, each country's domestic law applies.
facts.locator: Paragraphs following the domestic residence criteria

facts.label: Residents and foreign income
facts.text: French tax residents are generally within income tax on French and foreign income, subject to international agreements. Foreign income is not automatically outside French reporting merely because it was earned abroad.
facts.locator: Conséquences fiscales si vous êtes fiscalement domicilié en France; resident income scope

facts.label: Non-residents and French income
facts.text: Non-residents report French-source income taxable in France under the relevant treaty, or domestic law where no treaty applies. Do not turn this into a claim that all French payments are taxed identically.
facts.locator: Si vous êtes non-résident

facts.label: Mixed-residence couples
facts.text: Residence is determined for each household member. One spouse can be resident while the other is non-resident; household reporting then depends on marital arrangements and treaty rules.
facts.locator: Le couple mixte

limits: No universal 183-day safe harbour or nationality-based exemption is asserted.
Rates, wealth or property taxes, social charges, special territorial rules and precise household filing instructions are outside this baseline.

topics.title: Germany Tax Residence and Foreign Income
topics.summary: Germany's ordinary individual income-tax scope follows a residence or habitual abode, with treaties and special statutory cases considered separately.
topics.scope: Selected ordinary individual residence and income-scope rules; not a calculation of rates, exit tax, extended limited liability or treaty entitlement.

facts.label: A retained home can establish residence
facts.text: An individual with a German residence or habitual abode generally has unlimited income-tax liability. A residence is a dwelling held in circumstances indicating it will be retained and used; it is not simply a citizenship test.
facts.locator: EStG section 1(1); AO section 8

facts.label: More than six months, with exceptions
facts.text: A continuous stay exceeding six months normally establishes habitual abode from its beginning, ignoring short interruptions. This specific rule excludes visits solely for recreation, treatment or comparable private purposes lasting no more than a year; a separate residence can still matter.
facts.locator: AO sections 8 and 9

facts.label: Worldwide-income baseline
facts.text: Unlimited income-tax liability generally covers worldwide income. The Ministry of Finance contrasts this with limited liability on domestic-source income; applicable treaty relief must still be examined.
facts.locator: An ABC of Taxes, printed page 61 (PDF page 61), Income tax; double-taxation guidance

facts.label: Non-residents can remain taxable
facts.text: Without a German residence or habitual abode, specified German-source income can attract limited liability. Section 1 also contains special public-service and application-based cases, so leaving is not a universal exemption.
facts.locator: EStG section 1(2)–(4), referring to section 49

facts.label: Use the relevant agreement
facts.text: Double-taxation agreements allocate taxing rights where domestic claims overlap. Consult the relevant country agreement rather than assuming that foreign income is automatically exempt or taxed twice.
facts.locator: Explanation of double-taxation agreements and links to authoritative texts

limits: The six-month habitual-abode rule is not a universal 183-day exemption from German taxation.
This baseline excludes rates, social insurance, church tax, departure taxation and special anti-avoidance cases.

topics.title: UAE Tax Residence and Business Income
topics.summary: UAE domestic tax residence has alternative tests. Individuals conducting business must separately consider corporate-tax rules and exclusions.
topics.scope: Natural-person domestic residence and selected corporate-tax scope; not a treaty-residence certificate, immigration entitlement or personal liability calculation.
topics.jurisdiction: United Arab Emirates: natural-person tax residence and business taxation

facts.label: Domestic residence alternatives
facts.text: One test concerns the UAE being both the usual or primary residence and centre of financial and personal interests. Another requires at least 183 days of physical presence within the relevant 12 consecutive months.
facts.locator: Cabinet Decision 85/2022, Article 4(1)–(2), PDF page 2

facts.label: The 90-day route has extra conditions
facts.text: At least 90 days in the relevant 12 consecutive months can qualify only with UAE nationality, GCC nationality or a valid UAE residence permit, plus a permanent UAE home or UAE employment or business. A visitor entry permit is not the defined residence permit.
facts.locator: Articles 1 and 4(3), PDF pages 1–3

facts.label: Days and an available home
facts.text: The implementing guidance counts any part of a day spent in the UAE. A permanent place of residence need not be owned, but must be continuously available.
facts.locator: Ministerial Decision 27/2023 implementation explanation

facts.label: Corporate tax can apply to individuals
facts.text: FTA states that a natural person falls within corporate tax when conducting UAE business or business activities whose total turnover exceeds AED 1 million in a calendar year. This is a turnover test, not a statement that every dirham of turnover is taxable profit.
facts.locator: Basis of Taxation – Natural Person: two qualifying conditions

facts.label: Wages and personal investment categories
facts.text: For that natural-person business test, FTA excludes wages, personal investment income and real-estate investment income from business activities. Classification matters; a commercial activity is not exempt merely because an individual conducts it.
facts.locator: Income streams not considered Business or Business Activities

facts.label: Treaty residence is a separate check
facts.text: An international agreement's own residence conditions apply for that agreement. Meeting a domestic test is therefore not a promise of treaty benefits or exemption from another country's obligations.
facts.locator: Article 6, PDF page 3

limits: The authority-hosted English Cabinet Decision is expressly labelled an unofficial translation; the governing Arabic text prevails.
Business-income scope is not citizenship eligibility. Treaty claims, corporate-tax relief, rates, VAT and other countries' obligations require separate assessment.

review.notes: Independently opened and read all 13 cited primary authorities for the 21 facts across PT, FR, DE and AE tax topics. Portuguese Articles 15 and 16 support the strictly-more-than-183-day threshold, overnight counting, home alternative, part-year qualifications and nationality-linked listed-jurisdiction departure exception; the candidate does not infer special-regime eligibility. French current guidance supports alternative household/activity/economic-interest criteria, treaty priority, resident and non-resident income scope and individual assessment within mixed-residence couples. Read German EStG section 1, AO sections 8 and 9, and the Finance Ministry treaty guidance; directly fetched AO section 8 after the browser timeout. Independently downloaded and visually inspected printed/PDF page 61 of the 2025 ABC of Taxes, confirming the individual worldwide-income passage and locator. The habitual-abode exception and separate retained-home test are preserved. topics.title: Japan Citizenship Requirements
topics.summary: Japan's five-year statutory domicile condition and the stricter ten-year integration assessment introduced in April 2026 are different requirements.
topics.scope: Selected ordinary adult naturalisation requirements, including the assessment policy effective 1 April 2026; not special family, birth or former-national routes.

facts.label: Five-year statutory minimum
facts.text: Article 5 sets a minimum of five consecutive years domiciled in Japan with valid residence status. Meeting this statutory condition does not guarantee permission: the newer integration assessment below must also be considered.
facts.locator: Nationality Q9(1); minister's explanation of the unchanged five-year statutory condition

constraint.cohort: Ordinary Article 5 domicile minimum, not the complete current assessment or approval timeline

facts.label: Ten-year assessment policy from April 2026
facts.text: From 1 April 2026, the Ministry generally requires at least ten years of residence when assessing integration into Japanese society. This is a discretionary assessment policy, not an amendment replacing Article 5's five-year minimum. Individual cases remain subject to assessment.
facts.locator: 27 March announcement and questions on stricter assessment; Asahikawa integration paragraph

facts.label: Practical Japanese ability
facts.text: Current Legal Affairs Bureau guidance requires Japanese conversation, reading and writing sufficient for everyday life. It does not establish a JLPT or CEFR level here; no equivalence is inferred.
facts.locator: Integration paragraph following the Article 6–8 exceptions

facts.label: Age, conduct and livelihood
facts.text: Ordinary applicants must be at least 18 and legally capable under their home law. Conduct, tax compliance and a stable family-unit livelihood matter. The April 2026 policy also lengthens the reviewed history of tax and social-insurance payments without specifying a duration in the announcement.
facts.locator: Nationality Q9(2)–(4); 27 March announcement on payment-history review

facts.label: Existing nationality normally must be lost
facts.text: Applicants normally must be stateless or lose their former nationality on naturalisation. An exception may apply where losing it is beyond their control. This is not an unrestricted dual-citizenship route.
facts.locator: Nationality Q9(5), Article 5(2) exception

facts.label: Local bureau and individual permission
facts.text: Apply personally in writing to the Legal Affairs Bureau responsible for the home address, with identity and eligibility evidence. Constitutional-compliance conditions also apply; nationality begins when the permission is announced in the Official Gazette.
facts.locator: Naturalisation definition; constitutional-compliance condition; application procedure

limits: Five years is not an assurance that an ordinary application will be approved under the current ten-year assessment policy.
Family-related relaxations, detailed evidence, prior applications and any individual exception require the responsible bureau's advice. No processing time or automatic entitlement is claimed.

topics.title: Japan Tax Residence and Foreign Income
topics.summary: Japan's individual tax framework distinguishes residence, non-permanent tax residence and non-residence; nationality affects one category but does not replace residence tests.
topics.scope: Baseline individual income-tax categories in NTA guidance as at 1 April 2026; not a remittance calculation, treaty opinion or immigration-status determination.

facts.label: Domicile or one year of residence
facts.text: A resident has a domicile in Japan or has continuously maintained a residence there for at least one year. Domicile means the objective centre of living, so residence can arise before a year has passed.
facts.locator: Domestic-law treatment: domicile and residence definitions

facts.label: A specific foreign-national category
facts.text: Non-permanent tax residence applies only to residents without Japanese nationality whose total Japanese domicile or residence was at most five years within the preceding ten years. It is an income-tax category, not an immigration permit.
facts.locator: Resident income scope, subsection (2) and classification table

facts.label: Ordinary residents and worldwide income
facts.text: Residents outside that non-permanent category are taxed on income arising both in and outside Japan. A Japanese national cannot use the foreign-national non-permanent category simply by recently returning.
facts.locator: Resident income scope, subsections (1) and (2)

facts.label: Non-permanent residents and foreign income
facts.text: Their taxable scope includes income other than statutory foreign-source income, plus foreign-source income paid in Japan or remitted there. This is not a blanket exemption for overseas earnings; source and remittance rules need individual analysis.
facts.locator: Resident income scope, subsection (2)

facts.label: Non-resident and treaty scope
facts.text: Non-residents are taxed on Japanese-source income. Applicable treaties can affect residence and taxing rights; the NTA describes treaty residence tie-breakers separately from the domestic test.
facts.locator: Non-resident income scope; treaty treatment

limits: Rates, local inhabitant taxes, social insurance, specific securities rules and filing deadlines are outside this baseline.
The passport does not by itself determine residence or the final tax bill.

topics.title: Switzerland Citizenship Requirements
topics.summary: Ordinary Swiss naturalisation combines federal residence and language conditions with cantonal and communal requirements and a permanent residence permit.
topics.scope: Selected ordinary naturalisation conditions for applications under the system effective from 1 January 2018; simplified family and restoration routes are separate.
topics.jurisdiction: Switzerland: federal, cantonal and communal citizenship

facts.label: Ten years and a C permit
facts.text: The ordinary route requires ten qualifying years, including three of the preceding five, and a C permanent residence permit. Qualifying residence between ages eight and eighteen counts double, but actual residence must still reach six years.
facts.locator: Ordinary naturalisation: when to apply; Article 9; federal requirements

constraint.cohort: Ordinary route; qualifying permits, youth double-counting and actual-residence minimum apply

facts.label: Not every permit counts equally
facts.text: B and C permits and FDFA legitimation or Ci documents count; F-permit time counts half. N asylum-procedure and L short-stay periods do not count. Local residence requirements add two to five years depending on canton and commune.
facts.locator: Federal and cantonal law requirements

facts.label: B1 oral language skills
facts.text: Federal rules require oral skills of at least CEFR B1 in a Swiss national language. Cantons can require more; attendance certificates and online placement tests alone are insufficient evidence.
facts.locator: Ordinary naturalisation: required language skills, Article 6 ordinance

facts.label: A2 written skills and accommodations
facts.text: The federal written-skills minimum is CEFR A2. Serious illness, disability or pronounced learning or literacy difficulties require supporting evidence; the authority decides how personal circumstances are accommodated.
facts.locator: Ordinary naturalisation: language requirements and medical-evidence question

facts.label: Integration and local approval
facts.text: Authorities assess integration, familiarity with Swiss life and security. Canton-specific conditions also matter. A federal licence precedes the final cantonal decision; citizenship follows when that decision is legally binding.
facts.locator: Federal naturalisation licence; cantonal naturalisation decision

facts.label: Swiss law permits dual nationality
facts.text: Swiss naturalisation does not require renouncing the prior citizenship under Swiss law. The other country's law can still cause its loss, so both legal systems must be checked.
facts.locator: Opening guidance on acquiring Swiss citizenship

limits: Federal minimums are not a complete cantonal or communal application checklist. Ask the authority where you live about accepted proof and extra requirements.
Residence eligibility is not processing time or a guarantee of approval; simplified routes require separate assessment.

topics.title: Switzerland Tax Residence and Income
topics.summary: Swiss individual taxation combines residence-based federal liability with cantonal and communal income and wealth taxes. Location and cross-border income matter.
topics.scope: Selected individual-tax foundations from the FTA's 2025 system guide and 2026 official updates; not a canton-specific rate calculation or treaty assessment.
topics.jurisdiction: Switzerland: federal, cantonal and communal individual taxes

facts.label: Residence creates broad liability
facts.text: The FTA describes unlimited liability through personal tax residence. A stay can establish residence after at least 30 days with gainful work or 90 days without it, ignoring temporary interruptions. These are not substitutes for assessing domicile.
facts.locator: Section 8.1.1.1, printed page 28 (PDF page 30)

facts.label: Swiss economic links can remain taxable
facts.text: Without Swiss domicile or residence, Swiss business operations, a permanent establishment or real estate can still create limited tax liability. Non-residence is not a blanket exemption.
facts.locator: Section 8.1.1.1, printed page 28 (PDF page 30)

facts.label: Income and wealth at different levels
facts.text: Federal tax covers individual income, not individual wealth. Cantons and communes also levy income and wealth taxes. Wealth assessments generally use net assets, with deductions and thresholds varying by canton.
facts.locator: Sections 8.1.1, 9.1.2 and 9.1.4; printed pages 27, 52 and 54

facts.label: Cross-border allocation matters
facts.text: Foreign property and business income require allocation rather than assuming every foreign receipt is exempt or fully taxable. Zurich's current guidance distinguishes personal and corporate cases and applies worldwide-income rate progression to individuals under the cited federal rules.
facts.locator: Sections 1.1 and 1.2, natural-person columns and rate rows; Articles 6 and 7 DBG

facts.label: Individual-tax reform is a future change
facts.text: The Federal Council announced in August 2026 that individual taxation will start in 2032. The announced reform must not be treated as a current replacement of household-assessment rules; canton-level implementation remains necessary.
facts.locator: 19 August 2026 release: implementation date and cantonal changes

limits: Tax residence, treaty allocation, withholding, wealth valuation and cantonal rates need personal review; no Swiss passport tax rate is implied.
The system guide is the stated 2025 edition, supplemented only by the cited 2026 updates. This is not a complete review of special regimes or later reforms.

review.notes: Independently opened all 11 cited official sources and checked all 22 facts in the four bounded topics. The three Japanese justice sources returned HTTP 200 through direct fetch after the web tool returned 403. The 27 March 2026 ministerial announcement expressly distinguishes the unchanged five-year statutory domicile condition from the generally ten-year integration assessment effective 1 April; the updated Asahikawa guidance corroborates that policy and practical Japanese conversation, reading and writing, without a claimed exam equivalence. Age, lawful residence, livelihood, conduct, nationality-loss exceptions and personal application remain qualified. NTA No. 2875 and No. 2010 identify their law date as 1 April 2026 and support the separate domicile/residence tests, foreign-national five-of-ten-year non-permanent tax category, remittance/source distinctions and treaty caveat. SEM sources support Swiss qualifying residence, three-of-five-year recency, C permit, youth credits, permit exclusions, cantonal variation, distinct B1 oral/A2 written minima, accommodations, final approval and dual-nationality qualification. Downloaded the FTA 2025 edition PDF and independently inspected text and rendered pages: printed page 28 is PDF page 30; printed 27, 52 and 54 support tax-level and wealth statements. Its residence thresholds are not presented as replacing domicile. The 5 March 2026 Zurich allocation tables distinguish natural from legal persons and support only the expressly scoped cross-border allocation/rate-progression statement. The 19 August 2026 FTA announcement supports 2032 as a future individual-tax reform, not current rules. Scope and limitations preserve the stated editions and do not assert personal eligibility, complete tax liability, guaranteed processing or a passport-dependent tax rate. No candidate or production data was edited by this reviewer; approval binds only the exact candidate bytes and does not constitute deployment approval.

topics.title: Netherlands Citizenship Requirements
topics.summary: Dutch ordinary naturalisation combines five years of qualifying residence with integration, suitable residence status and normally renunciation of other citizenships.
topics.scope: Selected ordinary adult naturalisation requirements for residents applying through a Netherlands municipality; option, overseas and shortened family routes are separate.
topics.jurisdiction: Kingdom of the Netherlands: Dutch nationality

facts.label: Five consecutive qualifying years
facts.text: The ordinary baseline is five consecutive years in the Kingdom with lawful residence and timely permit extensions. Exceptions allow earlier applications; five years is an eligibility condition, not a processing-time promise.
facts.locator: Requirements: consecutive residence and exceptions to the five-year term

constraint.cohort: Ordinary adult route; continuous qualifying residence, with separate statutory exceptions

facts.label: Qualifying status throughout the process
facts.text: At application, during processing and at the ceremony, an accepted residence status is required. These include permanent residence, a non-temporary purpose, qualifying EU-family residence, EU-law residence and Withdrawal Agreement status; not every temporary permit qualifies.
facts.locator: Requirements: listed residence categories and validity at ceremony

facts.label: A2 Dutch and civic integration
facts.text: IND requires integration at at least A2, covering reading, listening, writing and speaking alongside civic components. Accepted diplomas and formal exemptions or dispensations can satisfy or modify the exam requirement; these need supporting evidence.
facts.locator: What is the civic integration requirement; exam components; exemptions and dispensations

facts.label: Adult identity and public-order checks
facts.text: Applicants must be at least 18, establish identity and nationality, and not threaten public order or national security. The municipality checks the application and supporting documents before IND assessment.
facts.locator: Requirements; process step 3

facts.label: Renunciation with defined exceptions
facts.text: Adults normally renounce other citizenships after becoming Dutch. Exceptions include a Dutch spouse or registered partner at the decree date and specified protection statuses. Other nationality laws can still cause automatic loss; assess each nationality before applying.
facts.locator: Renouncing nationality is required; exceptions; country list

facts.label: Approval is not the final step
facts.text: After approval and the Royal Decree, attend the naturalisation ceremony and make the declaration of solidarity. IND requires attendance within one year of the positive decision; the approval letter alone does not grant citizenship.
facts.locator: After the positive decision: Royal Decree, obligatory ceremony, declaration

limits: The IND requirements reviewed in September 2026 still state five years and A2. No proposed longer residence period or higher language level is substituted for current requirements.
Option, minor, family and overseas routes and Caribbean examination arrangements need their own assessment. This is not a complete personal application checklist.

topics.title: Netherlands Tax Residence and Foreign Income
topics.summary: Dutch resident and non-resident obligations differ. Worldwide income reporting does not mean every foreign receipt is ultimately taxed twice.
topics.scope: Baseline individual income-tax guidance for moving to, living in or earning income from the European Netherlands; no treaty-residence ruling or rate calculation.

facts.label: Moving to live in the Netherlands
facts.text: The Tax Administration's immigration guidance treats a move to live in the Netherlands as the start of resident-taxpayer status. Before the move, a person may be non-resident or outside Dutch tax scope. A passport is not a substitute for assessing the actual situation.
facts.locator: Your tax liability changes

facts.label: Worldwide reporting and treaty relief
facts.text: Residents report Dutch and foreign income. Whether the foreign portion is taxed in the Netherlands depends on applicable allocation and relief rules; reporting worldwide income is not the same as owing Dutch tax on every component.
facts.locator: Filing a tax return: worldwide income and double tax relief

facts.label: Dutch-source obligations can remain
facts.text: Non-residents report income taxable in the Netherlands, with treaty exemptions assessed separately. Dutch real estate and related rights can remain in scope; non-resident box 3 treatment does not generally include a Dutch bank account merely because it is Dutch.
facts.locator: Filing as a non-resident; state your property in box 3

facts.label: Returns and insurance are separate checks
facts.text: The migration year has a dedicated return procedure. Even without a filing letter, check whether tax is due or refundable. National-insurance and healthcare contributions depend on social-insurance coverage, not simply citizenship.
facts.locator: Your tax liability changes; filing an income tax return; social security

limits: This does not resolve disputed or dual tax residence, an expatriate concession, box 3 litigation or annual rates. Obtain case-specific advice for those questions.
Caribbean tax jurisdictions, corporate tax, inheritance and gift tax are not covered by this European-Netherlands income-tax baseline.

topics.title: New Zealand Citizenship Requirements
topics.summary: New Zealand's usual citizenship-by-grant route requires five years as a qualifying resident, specific physical presence, basic English and good character.
topics.scope: Selected usual adult citizenship-by-grant requirements; not citizenship by birth or descent, special Samoan provisions or discretionary waivers.

facts.label: Five years as a qualifying resident
facts.text: Ordinarily, the preceding five years must be under status allowing indefinite residence. Any resident-visa conditions must be met or cancelled. Australian citizens and permanent residents also need five years living in New Zealand under this guidance.
facts.locator: Presence requirement 1: residence visas, multiple permits and Australian residents

constraint.cohort: Ordinary grant route: qualifying indefinite residence, not five years on any visa

facts.label: 1,350 days and a yearly minimum
facts.text: Within the five years counted back from application, presence as a resident must reach 1,350 days overall and at least 240 days in each twelve-month period. Meeting only the overall total is insufficient.
facts.locator: Presence requirement 2: overall and each twelve-month period

constraint.cohort: Ordinary grant route; also at least 240 days in each twelve-month period

facts.label: Intention to remain connected
facts.text: Applicants normally intend to keep living in New Zealand. Specified overseas employment or accompanying a New Zealand spouse or partner on Crown service can qualify instead; ordinary plans to settle abroad are not automatically equivalent.
facts.locator: Presence requirement 3; planning to live outside New Zealand

facts.label: Basic conversational English
facts.text: Applicants need basic conversational English. Non-native speakers provide accepted evidence such as school, employment or language-test records; a case officer may interview them. No fixed IELTS score or CEFR level is asserted by this guidance.
facts.locator: Opening requirement; if English is not your first language

facts.label: Character and disclosure
facts.text: Good character is assessed separately. Pending charges, recent convictions, imprisonment, protection orders and other specified conduct can affect approval. Required disclosures and any requested overseas police clearances must not be omitted.
facts.locator: Crimes and investigations; declarations; overseas residence

facts.label: Citizenship test planned for late 2027
facts.text: Currently applicants declare that they understand citizenship responsibilities and privileges. A test is planned for most grant applications from late 2027, not current applications. The reviewed announcement does not yet fix the exact start date or final procedural details.
facts.locator: Opening announcement; about the citizenship test

limits: Residence, physical presence and processing time are different measures. Individual waivers, children and special Samoan routes require separate assessment.
Recheck the announced 2027 test before applying; no exact effective date is invented and it is not presented as a current requirement.

topics.title: New Zealand Tax Residence and Foreign Income
topics.summary: New Zealand generally taxes residents on worldwide income, with separate rules for transitional residents, qualifying visitors and non-resident source income.
topics.scope: Selected individual residence and income-scope rules, including Inland Revenue's June 2026 visitor and transitional-residence guidance; not a personal tax determination.

facts.label: Home ties or more than 183 days
facts.text: Residence generally begins at a permanent place of abode or more than 183 days in any twelve months, whichever occurs first. Partial days count as present; the day test backdates residence. Qualifying non-resident visitors and specified workers have exceptions.
facts.locator: Becoming resident; day counting; permanent place of abode; seasonal workers

facts.label: A tightly qualified visitor exception
facts.text: The visitor rule allows up to 275 days in any eighteen-month period only if all conditions hold: not a New Zealand tax or transitional resident before qualifying; not working for or paid by a New Zealand resident or a non-resident employer's New Zealand branch; no local sales or location-dependent work; neither partner receives Working for Families; lawful presence; and tax liability in another country of residence.
facts.locator: Non-resident visitors: all listed conditions

facts.label: Leaving does not immediately end residence
facts.text: Ordinary non-residence requires both no permanent place of abode and more than 325 days absent in twelve months, with specific counting and backdating rules. Overseas New Zealand-government service has a separate continuing-residence rule.
facts.locator: Knowing when you become non-resident; counting days; government service

facts.label: Residents generally report worldwide income
facts.text: Foreign income is generally taxable even if retained abroad or already taxed overseas. Foreign-tax credits and treaties may provide relief; overseas-employer salary is not automatically exempt.
facts.locator: How worldwide income is taxed; double tax agreements; employment

facts.label: One-off transitional exemption
facts.text: Eligible new or returning residents with no New Zealand tax residence in the preceding ten years can receive a one-off exemption for most foreign income for roughly four years. Foreign employment and personal-services income are excluded. Opting out or specified Working for Families applications can end it early; exact dates require separate calculation.
facts.locator: Qualifying; early ending; exempt and non-exempt income; start and end dates

facts.label: New Zealand source income still matters
facts.text: Non-residents generally remain taxable on New Zealand-source income. Withholding can apply to interest, dividends and royalties; treaties and the kind of income affect liability and whether a return is required.
facts.locator: Opening rule; double tax agreements; withholding; filing

limits: Tax residence is different from nationality and immigration permission. The visitor exception is not blanket tax-free remote-work permission.

Property-sale rules, investment-fund calculations, tax rates, trusts and superannuation are outside this baseline. Confirm current rules and personal treaty treatment with Inland Revenue or a qualified adviser.

review.notes: Independently opened all 14 official sources and reviewed the 22 facts in four topics. The two Govt.nz presence/language pages returned HTTP 200 through direct fetch after web-tool errors; all other authorities were read through the web tool. Current IND guidance supports five consecutive qualifying years, accepted status throughout processing and ceremony, A2 integration with exceptions, adult identity/conduct checks, qualified renunciation and the required ceremony after approval. Proposed higher thresholds are not substituted for current requirements. Dutch tax guidance supports scoped immigration-year, worldwide-reporting, relief and non-resident asset statements without asserting a treaty outcome. New Zealand guidance supports five years of indefinite-residence status, 1,350 resident-presence days AND 240 in each twelve-month period, qualified intention, basic conversational English and character disclosure. The announced late-2027 test remains future with no invented exact date. Required correction was made to the NZ visitor-tax fact: the draft's lifetime-sounding prior-residence exclusion is now the source's not-resident-before-qualifying condition; working for or being paid by a New Zealand resident or qualifying branch is preserved, and the window is any eighteen-month period. IRD's June 2026 residence guidance supports the separate abode and strict more-than-183/more-than-325-day rules, counting/backdating, visitor conditions and government-service exception. Transitional relief remains one-off, approximately four years, conditional and excludes foreign employment/personal-services income; resident and non-resident income rules retain treaty qualifications. No individual eligibility, guaranteed timetable, immigration permission or blanket tax exemption is asserted. Approval binds these exact candidate bytes only. Reviewer changed only this review file, not the candidate or production artifacts; deployment remains outside this approval.

topics.title: Sweden Citizenship Requirements
topics.summary: Sweden's ordinary adult citizenship requirements changed in June 2026: eight years is the general residence baseline, alongside knowledge, support and conduct requirements.
topics.scope: Selected ordinary adult citizenship-by-application conditions after the June and July 2026 changes; not Nordic notification, child or special shortened routes.

facts.label: Eight years is the current general rule
facts.text: The general baseline is eight continuous years of habitual residence. The June 2026 changes also apply to undecided earlier applications. Nordic, family, refugee, stateless and other specified cases have different requirements; the shortest exception is not the ordinary baseline.
facts.locator: Requirements following 6 June 2026; how long must you have lived in Sweden

constraint.cohort: Ordinary habitual-residence baseline after 6 June 2026; qualifying residence and exceptions apply

facts.label: Qualifying residence and absences
facts.text: Visitor, ordinary study and au-pair time generally do not count; qualifying doctoral study can. If absence exceeds six weeks in a year, all time abroad that year is deducted. Settling abroad ends the continuous period.
facts.locator: Habitual residence: permits not included; doctoral study; travel abroad

facts.label: Residence status and July exceptions
facts.text: Permanent residence or an accepted residence right/status is normally required. From 12 July, specified temporary-permit holders can qualify, including protection and associated family categories, generally with well-founded long-term prospects. A valid permit is still needed; an extension application alone is insufficient for this exception.
facts.locator: Listed temporary permits; long-term prospects; application requirements

facts.label: B1 reading and listening
facts.text: For the knowledge requirement, ordinarily applying from ages 16–66, reading and listening are CEFR B1. Approved qualifications can establish competence; Nordic and specified stateless applicants and individual disability-related cases have exemptions.
facts.locator: Knowledge requirement: ages, exemptions and recognised Swedish qualifications

facts.label: A2 speaking and writing
facts.text: Speaking and writing are CEFR A2, not B1. Swedish-society knowledge is also required. The separate Swedish-language citizenship test is not expected before autumn 2027; current applicants use recognised education or accepted proficiency tests instead.
facts.locator: Recognised language qualifications; society knowledge; citizenship-test transition

facts.label: Own income, with exemptions
facts.text: The maintenance rule generally requires sustainable employment or self-employment income of at least three income base amounts annually, not combined partner income. Specified pensioners, successful full-time students and disability cases can be exempt; disallowed benefits and past social assistance also matter.
facts.locator: Support yourself; income that does not count; exemptions

facts.label: Identity and conduct assessment
facts.text: Identity documents and personal appearance support identity verification. Conduct inside and outside Sweden, debts and offences are assessed; waiting periods can apply after debts or sentences are resolved. Approval remains individual.
facts.locator: Identity verification; orderly and respectable life; debts and criminal offences

facts.label: Sweden allows multiple citizenship
facts.text: Swedish law permits retaining earlier citizenship when becoming Swedish, but the other nationality's law may cause loss or impose restrictions. Swedish permission does not settle the other country's rules.
facts.locator: Dual and multiple citizenship

limits: Habitual residence is not simply time holding any permit, and an eligibility period is not a processing estimate.
This captures the reviewed 2026 rules, not the older five-year/no-language baseline. Exam availability, exemptions and each applicant's permit history require current authority confirmation.

topics.title: Sweden Tax Residence and Foreign Income
topics.summary: Swedish individual tax scope depends on residence, continuing connections and income source. Moving abroad does not necessarily end worldwide-income obligations.
topics.scope: Baseline individual limited/unlimited tax liability and selected non-resident procedures; not annual rates, treaty advice or a personal exit assessment.

facts.label: Residence, regular stay or significant ties
facts.text: Unlimited liability can arise from actual residence, a regular stay of six consecutive months or more, or significant connections after leaving. Short visits abroad do not necessarily interrupt a regular stay; fewer than 183 days is not a universal exemption.
facts.locator: Liability for taxation: three connections and regular stay

facts.label: Worldwide income with relief rules
facts.text: Unlimited liability generally covers Swedish and foreign income. Domestic exemptions and treaties can reduce taxation, but the authority still requires disclosure of income in applicable returns. Liability and final tax payable are different questions.
facts.locator: Worldwide income, domestic rules, treaties and disclosure

facts.label: Five-year evidential rule after departure
facts.text: Swedish citizens and people resident for at least ten years must establish that close ties have ended during the first five years after departure. Home, family and business connections matter. Continuing ties can sustain residence even after five years; this is not an automatic five-year tax holiday or fixed end date.
facts.locator: Five years from departure; examples of close ties; treatment after five years

facts.label: Limited liability still covers specified income
facts.text: People outside unlimited liability can still owe Swedish tax on specified Swedish income. Eligible non-residents working briefly in Sweden or receiving a Swedish pension may apply for SINK; an authority decision is needed, and ordinary income-tax treatment can be elected instead.
facts.locator: Limited taxation; SINK eligibility and decisions; election under Income Tax Act

limits: This does not calculate SINK, municipal or national rates. The SINK page contains a 2026 rate-change notice alongside older examples; no stale example rate is imported.
Treaty residence, foreign-tax relief, pensions, investment gains and special worker rules require their own assessment. Citizenship alone does not decide all Swedish tax obligations.

review.notes: Independently opened and read all seven cited Swedish Migration Agency and Swedish Tax Agency sources. Verified the eight-year ordinary habitual-residence baseline and immediate application of the 6 June 2026 amendments to undecided earlier applications; excluded permit periods, doctoral-study qualification and absence deductions; the 12 July temporary-permit exceptions, generally applicable long-term prospects condition and need for a valid permit. The detailed authority expressly supports CEFR B1 reading/listening and A2 speaking/writing, knowledge exemptions, society knowledge and the separate Swedish-language citizenship test expected no earlier than autumn 2027. Own-income maintenance, exceptions, identity, conduct and multiple nationality are supported within the selected adult-route scope. Tax evidence supports residence/regular-stay/significant-ties alternatives, worldwide income subject to domestic and treaty relief, the five-year evidential burden for specified emigrants without an automatic end to liability, and limited-liability/SINK procedures. The SINK page mixes a current rate-change notice and older rate text; the candidate correctly imports no rate. No candidate edits or publication changes were made. Approval is limited to these two topics and the exact recorded SHA-256, not individual eligibility, treaty entitlement or processing outcomes.

topics.title: Italy Citizenship Requirements
topics.summary: Italy's ordinary adult residence route generally requires ten years of legal residence for non-EU nationals, with shorter statutory cohorts, language proof and a discretionary grant process.
topics.scope: Adult residence-based naturalisation under Article 9 of Law 91/1992; descent recognition, marriage and exceptional-service grants are separate routes.

facts.label: Ordinary non-EU residence period
facts.text: The ordinary non-EU route requires at least ten years of legal residence in Italy. Citizenship may be granted by presidential decree on the Interior Minister's proposal; completing the period is not approval.
facts.locator: Opening paragraph and Article 9(1)(f)

constraint.cohort: Ordinary adult non-EU applicant without a shorter statutory route

facts.label: Shorter statutory cohorts
facts.text: EU citizens have a four-year legal-residence period; stateless applicants have five years. Other family, Italian-birth, adoption and state-service cohorts have separate conditions and must not be generalised to everyone.
facts.locator: Article 9(1)(a)–(e), including current two-year ancestry and three-year Italian-birth clauses

facts.label: Lawful and continuous residence
facts.text: Legal residence requires compliance with entry, stay and population-registration rules. The Prefecture's ordinary-route guidance requires continuous legal residence. This is not simply a total of days physically spent in Italy.
facts.locator: DPR 572/1993 Article 1(2)(a); Milan: Acquisto della cittadinanza per residenza legale ininterrotta in Italia

facts.label: Italian language and accepted proof
facts.text: Article 9 naturalisation normally requires Italian at least CEFR B1, shown by a recognised educational qualification or language certification. Integration-agreement signatories and holders of the specified EU long-term residence permit have statutory proof exemptions.
facts.locator: Judgment 25/2025, Considerato in diritto 4.1–4.3; Article 9.1 framework and proof alternatives

facts.label: Severe language-learning limitations
facts.text: Judgment 25/2025 requires exemption from language proof for severe learning limitations resulting from age, illness or disability, certified by a public health facility. Age alone is not the stated exemption.
facts.locator: Considerato in diritto 5.1 and operative decision, point 1

facts.label: Income and documentary checks
facts.text: The residence application requires birth, criminal-record, identity and residence-status evidence, subject to documented exceptions. Milan's guidance also requires qualifying income over the previous three years and permits specified family income to contribute.
facts.locator: Article 9 section: Occorre allegare all'istanza; Requisiti reddituali

facts.label: Multiple nationality and separate descent rules
facts.text: Italian law permits multiple citizenship, subject to applicable international agreements and the other country's law. The 2025 restrictions on automatic acquisition for people born abroad with another nationality are separate from this ordinary naturalisation route.
facts.locator: Sections 1, 2 introduction and 2.6; Law 91/1992 Article 11 and 2025 Article 3-bis reform

facts.label: Grant must be completed
facts.text: The grant normally takes effect only if the applicant swears loyalty and compliance with the Constitution and laws within six months of notification. A serious, established disability preventing the oath is exempted by constitutional judgment.
facts.locator: Law 91/1992 Article 10 and update (8), Constitutional Court judgment 258/2017

limits: This covers the ordinary adult residence route, not an assessment of an applicant's ancestry or eligibility. The eligibility period is not a processing estimate.

No universal permitted-absence allowance, separate physical-presence day count or separate civic-test exemption is established here. Confirm residence continuity and the complete current filing requirements with the competent Prefecture.

topics.title: Italy Individual Tax Context
topics.summary: Italy's baseline personal income tax distinguishes residents' worldwide income from non-residents' Italian-source income. Residence has alternative connections and cannot be determined from a passport or day count alone.
topics.scope: Baseline individual income-tax framework applicable on 17 September 2026; not a rate calculation, special new-resident regime or complete filing and foreign-asset reporting guide.

facts.label: Alternative residence tests
facts.text: A person is tax resident when, for most of the tax period, counting fractions of days, they have Italian civil-law residence, domicile, or physical presence. Domicile means the principal location of personal and family relationships. Individual tax periods are calendar years.
facts.locator: DPR 917/1986 Articles 2(2) and 7(1); Article 2 update (227), applicable from 1 January 2024

facts.label: Registration presumption
facts.text: Population-register entry for most of the tax period creates a rebuttable residence presumption. Being absent for much of the year does not by itself exclude the alternative residence or domicile tests.
facts.locator: DPR 917/1986 Article 2(2), final sentence and alternative connections

facts.label: Residents and foreign income
facts.text: The ordinary tax base for residents includes worldwide income, subject to deductions, exemptions, final withholding and substitute-tax rules. Foreign income is not generally outside Italian taxation merely because it arises abroad.

facts.label: Non-residents and Italian-source income
facts.text: Non-residents are taxed on Italian-source income. Source rules differ by category: Italian property, work performed in Italy, and specified Italian-paid pensions or investment income can be covered, with express exclusions.
facts.locator: DPR 917/1986 Article 3(1); Article 23(1)–(2)

facts.label: Foreign-tax relief and treaties
facts.text: Foreign income taxes paid definitively can qualify for a credit when the income enters the Italian tax base, within statutory limits and declaration conditions. Applicable double-tax agreements must also be checked; more favourable domestic rules remain available under Article 169.

facts.label: Certain Italian citizens moving abroad
facts.text: A separate rebuttable residence rule concerns Italian citizens removed from the resident register who move to specified foreign jurisdictions. Its ministerial-list and transitional provisions require checking; this is not a general worldwide tax on every Italian passport holder.
facts.locator: DPR 917/1986 Article 2(2-bis) and update (133), preserving the earlier rule pending the stated implementing decree

facts.label: Enacted consolidation starts in 2027
facts.text: The income-tax consolidation approved by Legislative Decree 117/2026 applies from 1 January 2027. Its repeal of the former TUIR provisions is deferred to that date; the preceding facts use the law applicable in September 2026.
facts.locator: Annex Article 376(1)(e), read with Article 377(1); enacted-future application, not a current replacement

limits: General information, not personal tax advice. Residence, income category, exemptions, treaty entitlement and reporting duties require individual analysis; consult the tax authority or a qualified adviser.

Special new-resident and inbound-worker regimes are outside this baseline. The foreign-jurisdiction list governing the citizenship-linked residence presumption was not independently resolved here. Recheck the 2027 consolidation before using this profile for later periods.

topics.title: Spain Citizenship Requirements
topics.summary: Spain's ordinary nationality-by-residence route requires ten years of legal, continuous residence immediately before applying. Reduced periods, integration evidence and renunciation exceptions depend on the applicant's cohort.
topics.scope: Ordinary adult nationality by residence; reduced statutory cohorts are distinguished from the baseline, and descent, option and exceptional grants are not fully covered.

facts.label: Ordinary legal residence
facts.text: The baseline is ten years of legal, continuous residence immediately before the application. It is not a physical-presence day total or a processing estimate.
facts.locator: Civil Code Article 22(1) and (3)

constraint.cohort: Ordinary adult applicant outside a reduced-period cohort

facts.label: Reduced periods are cohort-specific
facts.text: Recognised refugees need five years. Two years applies to nationals by origin of Ibero-American countries, Andorra, the Philippines, Equatorial Guinea or Portugal, and Sephardic applicants. Article 22(2) defines separate one-year birth, option, guardianship and family cohorts.
facts.locator: Civil Code Article 22(1)–(3); all periods retain legal, continuous, immediately preceding residence

facts.label: Conduct and grant decision
facts.text: Good civic conduct and sufficient integration must be proved. The Justice Minister may refuse for reasoned public-order or national-interest grounds.
facts.locator: Civil Code Articles 21(2) and 22(4)

facts.label: Spanish language and civic knowledge
facts.text: Ordinarily, applicants must pass DELE Spanish at CEFR A2 or higher and the CCSE constitutional and sociocultural test. Listed nationality exemptions, a prior qualifying DELE diploma and specified official educational certificates can replace the language examination; the two-year residence cohort is not identical to the DELE-exempt cohort.
facts.locator: Royal Decree 1004/2015 preamble (CEFR), Article 6(1), (5), (7)–(8), and additional provision four

facts.label: Waivers and accessible examinations
facts.text: Disability accommodations are available. Applicants unable to read or write or with learning difficulties may request a waiver before applying; it is not automatic. Those schooled in Spain who completed compulsory secondary education can submit the relevant proof with the nationality application without a prior waiver request.
facts.locator: Order JUS/1625/2016 Article 10(5), as amended by Order JUS/1018/2022

facts.label: Renunciation and treaty exceptions
facts.text: A renunciation declaration is generally required. Exceptions cover people from Ibero-American countries, Andorra, the Philippines, Equatorial Guinea and Portugal, Sephardic people originating from Spain, and French citizens under the bilateral convention. The French exception does not reduce the residence period; the other nationality's law must also be checked.
facts.locator: Instruction of 31 March 2022, introduction and section II.2 interpreting Civil Code Articles 23 and 24

facts.label: Oath and registration
facts.text: The required oath or promise, applicable nationality declaration and Civil Registry registration complete acquisition. A grant lapses if the required appearance is not made within 180 days after notification.
facts.locator: Civil Code Article 21(4) and Article 23

facts.label: Official application
facts.text: The Justice Ministry's electronic service accepts nationality-by-residence applications and supporting documents, with a separate service for requests to waive the Cervantes tests.
facts.locator: Solicitud de nacionalidad española por residencia; Solicitud de Dispensas de las pruebas del Instituto Cervantes

limits: No general safe absence allowance is established by this review. Residence continuity, the exact reduced-period category and documentary proof require individual review.
Renunciation declarations do not determine another country's loss rules. This is an acquisition-route summary, not a complete account of later nationality-retention duties or a promise of approval.

topics.title: Spain Individual Tax Context
topics.summary: Spain normally taxes resident individuals on worldwide income and non-residents on Spanish-source income. Residence depends on presence or economic connections, with family presumptions, nationality-linked exceptions and treaty rules.
topics.scope: Baseline individual IRPF and IRNR framework; not a tax-rate comparison, full regional or wealth-tax guide, or determination of eligibility for a special inbound regime.
topics.jurisdiction: Spanish personal income tax (IRPF) and non-resident income tax (IRNR)

facts.label: Presence or economic centre
facts.text: Residence can arise from more than 183 days in Spain during the calendar year or the main centre of activities or economic interests in Spain. Sporadic absences count unless foreign tax residence is proved. Shorter presence alone does not establish non-residence.
facts.locator: Normativa interna, first two residence tests and absence rule

facts.label: Family presumption and residence evidence
facts.text: Habitual Spanish residence of a non-separated spouse and dependent minor children creates a rebuttable presumption. A residence permit and tax residence are not the same status.
facts.locator: Normativa interna, family presumption; Acreditación de la residencia fiscal

facts.label: Residents' foreign income
facts.text: Ordinary IRPF residents are taxed on worldwide income, subject to applicable double-tax agreements. The tax period is the calendar year, and an ordinary residence change does not split it. Special inbound regimes have separate conditions and are outside this baseline.
facts.locator: Clases de contribuyentes en la imposición sobre la renta; Régimen especial de los trabajadores, profesionales, emprendedores e inversores desplazados

facts.label: Non-residents' Spanish income
facts.text: Non-resident individuals can owe IRNR on Spanish-source income. Category-specific connections include work performed in Spain, Spanish property income and certain dividends or pensions; treaty provisions and statutory exclusions still matter.
facts.locator: Tax overview: Clases de contribuyentes; source-income guidance items 2, 3, 5 and 6

facts.label: Specific nationality-linked continuation
facts.text: Spanish nationals moving to a non-cooperative jurisdiction remain IRPF taxpayers for the year of the move and four following tax periods. Specified Spanish diplomatic and public-service cases abroad also have special rules and exceptions; this is not universal citizenship-based taxation.
facts.locator: Normativa interna, Spanish-national relocation rule and note (1); Supuestos especiales

facts.label: Dual residence and treaties
facts.text: Where domestic laws both claim residence, an applicable treaty may resolve the conflict through permanent home, closer personal and economic ties, habitual abode, nationality and ultimately competent-authority agreement. Check the actual treaty rather than assuming a uniform exemption.
facts.locator: Convenio y doble residencia, criteria 1–5

limits: General information, not personal tax advice. Income categories, treaty relief, filing obligations and any regional rules require the tax authority or a qualified adviser.
Foreign-asset reporting, wealth taxes, special inbound regimes and individual treaty outcomes are not comprehensively reviewed here.

review.notes: Independently opened and read the relevant text of all 22 cited official sources. Normattiva date-pinned article bodies, Milan Prefecture guidance and selected BOE provisions were read through direct public HTTP retrieval where browser extraction failed or was truncated. Verified Italy's ordinary ten-year legal-residence route, reduced cohorts, registration requirement, B1 proof alternatives and the separate language-learning and oath disability judgments. Kept the 2025 automatic-acquisition reform distinct from ordinary naturalisation. Verified current TUIR residence, calendar period, tax base, source-income, credit and treaty provisions; the citizenship-linked presumption remains qualified because its current jurisdiction list was not established. Read Gazette Articles 376 and 377 together: replacement taxation provisions apply from 1 January 2027, not their 2026 publication date. Verified Spain Civil Code Articles 21–23, the actual additional provision four on educational language certificates (not the separate SICELE amendment), test-waiver rules, French renunciation exception without a shorter residence period, and the official application service. AEAT and the national administration support the scoped residence, worldwide/source-income and treaty facts. This approval concerns the four topics and exact candidate bytes only; it does not establish individual eligibility, all nationality-retention consequences, special tax regimes or a personal tax liability.

topics.title: Austria Citizenship Requirements
topics.summary: Austria's ordinary residence route separates ten years of lawful residence from five years of settlement, with language, support and nationality conditions.
topics.scope: Ordinary adult residence-based grant, with selected shorter-route distinctions. Not a determination of personal eligibility or every statutory exception.

facts.label: Ten years, including five settled
facts.text: The ordinary route requires ten lawful, uninterrupted years, including five with qualifying settlement status. Settlement is not identical to any residence permission or to permanent-residence status alone; the authority lists several qualifying permits.
facts.locator: Voraussetzungen; meanings of rechtmäßiger Aufenthalt and niedergelassen

constraint.cohort: Ordinary adult route, including five years with qualifying settlement status

facts.label: Absences and the decision date
facts.text: The guidance permits at most 20% of the relevant period outside Austria. Actual residence must be evidenced, and the period is assessed through the decision date, not frozen at application.
facts.locator: Ununterbrochener Aufenthalt

facts.label: Six years for defined cohorts
facts.text: Six qualifying years can suffice for EEA nationals, Austrian-born applicants, specified Austrian-spouse or registered-partner cases, B2 German, or demonstrated sustained integration. General naturalisation conditions still apply; none is an unconditional shortcut.
facts.locator: Voraussetzungen: six-year period and alternatives

facts.label: German and civic knowledge
facts.text: The ordinary language baseline is CEFR B1 through Module 2 or accepted equivalent evidence. A separate citizenship test covers democratic principles and Austrian and provincial history. Educational evidence and statutory exemptions require individual checking; B2 belongs to a shorter-route alternative.
facts.locator: Integrationsvereinbarung: Module and Modul 2; general knowledge requirements; six-year B2 alternative

facts.label: Support, conduct and application
facts.text: The ordinary support test uses qualifying regular income for 36 months within the preceding six years, including the final six months before application. Criminal, immigration and security conditions also apply. Apply personally to the competent provincial authority, which determines required documents.
facts.locator: Hinreichend gesicherter Lebensunterhalt; other prerequisites; Verfahrensablauf

facts.label: Previous nationality usually relinquished
facts.text: Applicants normally give up their prior nationality. Where it is not lost automatically, Austria generally first issues an assurance, followed by release within two years if possible and reasonable. Only the competent authority decides exceptions; do not renounce without checking the sequence.
facts.locator: Erwerb der österreichischen Staatsbürgerschaft durch ausländische Staatsangehörige

limits: This baseline does not exhaust disability, refugee, family, restitution, exceptional-merit or other statutory exceptions. Income sufficiency and acceptable evidence need authority assessment.
Austrian rules on voluntary acquisition of another nationality by an existing citizen are separate from this inbound naturalisation route. Check both nationality laws before taking action.

topics.title: Austria Tax Residence and Foreign Income
topics.summary: Austria connects ordinary personal income-tax liability to residence and habitual presence, with worldwide-income rules and treaty qualifications.
topics.scope: Baseline individual income-tax residence and source-income scope in the Finance Ministry's 2026 guidance. No personal tax calculation or special-regime recommendation.

facts.label: Home or habitual presence
facts.text: Unlimited liability can arise from a suitable dwelling used recurrently or habitual presence. After six months' presence it applies retrospectively. Citizenship is not decisive, and six months is not a universal tax-free allowance.
facts.locator: Unbeschränkte Steuerpflicht

facts.label: Worldwide income baseline
facts.text: Ordinary unlimited liability generally includes domestic and foreign income. Applicable treaty allocations and relief must still be checked; a general liability rule does not determine the final bill.
facts.locator: Welteinkommen; Doppelbesteuerungsabkommen

facts.label: Austrian income can remain taxable
facts.text: Without Austrian residence or habitual presence, Austrian-source income such as employment or specified pensions can still create limited liability. Qualifying EU/EEA taxpayers may elect different treatment; the election has its own income conditions.
facts.locator: Beschränkte Steuerpflicht; EU/EEA election

facts.label: Employment can affect the start date
facts.text: The guidance treats foreign employees with at least a six-month work permission or contract as unlimited taxpayers from arrival. Seasonal stays exceeding six months can also backdate liability. Border-worker treaty rules need separate assessment.
facts.locator: Foreign employees, seasonal employees and cross-border workers

limits: No rates, annual allowances, complete category-specific source rules, social-insurance treatment or eligibility for special relief are asserted. Residence and treaty facts must be checked for the individual.

review.notes: Independent review of the exact candidate bytes and research notes. All six cited official source pages were opened and their operative text read. Confirmed ordinary ten-year lawful residence including five years of qualifying settlement, not five years of permanent residence; the 20% absence limit and decision-date endpoint; CEFR B1 through Module 2 or accepted evidence versus B2 as a six-year alternative; qualified income, conduct and renunciation rules without generalising module-specific exemptions. Confirmed the Finance Ministry's 2026 home/habitual-presence and worldwide-income rules, treaty qualifications, limited-liability scope and conditional EU/EEA election, six-month retrospective treatment, and foreign-worker arrival-date rule. Candidate and review schemas, reviewer independence, hash and 90-day recheck interval validated. Approval is limited to the stated baseline and does not resolve individual eligibility, treaty outcomes or omitted special cases.
